faq.q: What subjects and topics does the formula sheet cover?
faq.a: It's split across four tabs: Math, Physics, Chemistry and Aptitude. Math spans algebra through calculus, coordinate geometry, probability and number theory; Physics runs from kinematics to modern physics and semiconductors; Chemistry covers atomic structure, equilibrium, organic named reactions and more; Aptitude includes number system, percentage, profit-loss, interest, time-speed-distance, clocks, calendars and shortcut tables. Each entry pairs the formula with a short concept note.

faq.q: Can I save formulas I keep needing and print just those?
faq.a: Yes. Tap the star (☆) on any formula to bookmark it; bookmarks are stored in your browser under the fs_bookmarks key and appear under the ⭐ Bookmarks tab. 'Print All' prints the whole sheet with a clean print stylesheet, while 'Print Bookmarks Only' switches to your bookmarks view and prints just those for exam-day revision.

faq.q: How does search work across the formulas?
faq.a: The search box filters by formula name, the expression itself, the topic, and the concept explanation, all case-insensitively, and highlights the matched text. Sections normally collapse when you click their headers, but during an active search they stay expanded so matching results across different topics are all visible at once.

faq.q: What is the 'Formula of the Day' at the top?
faq.a: It's a single highlighted formula chosen deterministically from the database using the current date (day number modulo the number of formulas), so everyone sees the same one on a given day and it changes daily. It shows the formula, its topic and the concept note — a small prompt to revise one thing you might not have searched for.
